visual_thesis: Domain metadata advertises a search endpoint whose output is retrieved content, not a generated answer.
mechanism_metaphor: A continuous folded-paper domain fabric fills the center, with three content leaves at left connected by nondirectional paper folds to a larger Search index. Above, Page metadata is a small exposed folded header that advertises Search endpoint at the upper-right edge of the same fabric. A single query arrow travels from a small Query fold at right to the physical endpoint port; no other arrowheads. From the endpoint a wide continuous fold opens downward into Retrieved Markdown, whose front leaf explicitly says Source references. This is retrieved evidence, not an answer-composing machine. Lower left Domain rules bounds the fabric without a security shield; the detached bottom-right qualifier says Not a generated answer. All content leaves that signify a collection share one informative front leaf, Website content. Keep the entire scene unframed, with many folds exposing collection, indexing, discovery and return relationships; never turn semantic regions into panels.
story_anchors: Page metadata enables visiting agents to discover and query a domain-owned search endpoint.
The endpoint returns source content in Markdown instead of composing an answer, subject to domain configurations and usage limits.

source_claim_map.proposition: Page metadata enables visiting agents to discover and query a domain-owned search endpoint.
The endpoint returns source content in Markdown instead of composing an answer, subject to domain configurations and usage limits.
The service crawls website pages, converts and indexes them; retrieval returns matched source material in Markdown.

excluded_claims: No universal correctness, security, health, adoption or productivity guarantee. No unsupported product controls, figures, data charts, simulated lettering or extra arrows.
No people, humanoids, logos, brands as decoration, photorealism, generic card boards or panel collages. Only exact allowlisted phrases once each; all other surfaces unmarked.
